program.name: Phase 3 Admin Catalog
program.description: The admin surface for the supply side: create and publish class offerings, schedule their occurrences, and see what has been booked — with every mutation recorded in staff_audit_log. Phase 2 built a working ordering system on top of offerings and occurrences that nothing could create.

technology.recurrence: Out of scope; one occurrence at a time
technology.capacityBelowBookings: Permitted, with a warning naming the booked count
technology.offeringTypes: CLASS only; ROOM and OPEN_PLAY are not bookable
technology.statusTransitions: Transition table in contracts, mirroring ORDER_TRANSITIONS
technology.auditTrail: staff_audit_log written inside each mutation's transaction
technology.mutationSurface: Server Actions gated on MANAGER via authenticatedAction

successCriteria.description: A manager can create a CLASS offering with a name, description, duration, capacity, and price, and it is saved as DRAFT.
Offering slugs are generated from the name and stay unique when two offerings share a name.
Publishing moves an offering DRAFT to PUBLISHED; archiving moves it to ARCHIVED; an undeclared transition is refused.
A manager can schedule an occurrence for a published offering, and ends_at is derived from the offering's duration.
Scheduling an occurrence in the past is refused with a clear message.
Two overlapping occurrences of the same offering are refused.
A scheduled occurrence of a published offering appears on /book with its seat count.
Lowering capacity below the booked count succeeds, warns the manager with the booked count, and leaves /book showing zero seats rather than a negative number.
Cancelling an unbooked occurrence succeeds; cancelling one with confirmed reservations is refused and states why.
Every catalog mutation writes a staff_audit_log row naming the actor, action, and entity.
An audit entry never survives a mutation that rolled back.
Every admin action rejects a caller whose role is below MANAGER.
/admin/offerings lists offerings with status and supports create, edit, publish, and archive.
/admin/schedules lists upcoming occurrences by day with booked counts, and supports scheduling and cancellation.
/admin/reservations shows who is booked on an occurrence, with participant names.
Playwright covers creating and publishing a class, scheduling it, and seeing it appear on /book.

packages.name: catalog-admin
packages.description: NEW. Write paths for offerings and occurrences: create, edit, guarded status transitions, scheduling, and cancellation, each recording a staff_audit_log entry in its own transaction. Separate from catalog-core, which stays a read-only customer-facing query package.

packages.name: contracts
packages.description: Adds the offering status transition table, admin input schemas that exclude derived fields, and the audit action constants and entry type.

packages.name: catalog-core
packages.description: Consumed unchanged; its read paths are what the admin surface's booked counts and the customer page both rely on.

packages.name: reservation-core
packages.description: Consumed unchanged; supplies the reservation and participant reads behind /admin/reservations and the booked counts that gate cancellation.

packages.name: database
packages.description: Consumed unchanged; offerings, occurrences, and staff_audit_log all already exist. This program is the first writer of staff_audit_log.

packages.name: auth
packages.description: Consumed unchanged; the admin actions pass MANAGER to the existing authorize predicate.

packages.name: web
packages.description: The three admin surfaces and their Server Actions, replacing placeholders.

packages.name: ui
packages.description: Presentational primitives for the admin surfaces: status badges, form fields, and the occurrence list.

workstreams.name: Contracts: offering status transitions, admin input schemas, audit types
catalog-admin: offering create, edit, and guarded status transitions
catalog-admin: occurrence scheduling, edit, and cancellation
Audit logging: transactional staff_audit_log writes for every mutation
Admin Server Actions with the MANAGER boundary

outOfScope: Recurring schedules or a series concept
Cancelling occurrences that have confirmed reservations
Refunds, and any dependency on refundPayment
Deleting offerings or occurrences; archive and cancel are the exits
Editing or moving an existing reservation, and check-in
Image or media upload for offerings
An audit-log viewer; this program writes entries, it does not display them
